meta.title: Keep Slack Active All Day — Green Bean
meta.description: Keep your Slack green dot on during work hours. Your status stays active even with your laptop closed, and switches off automatically when the day ends. 14-day free trial.

hero.lead: Close your laptop, take lunch, and your Slack green dot stays on. Green Bean holds your status active during the hours you set and stops Slack from flipping you to away. Configure it once — the cloud handles the rest.

features.title: Why Green Bean
features.sub: No more mouse jigglers, no more leaving a window open just to look online.

real.title: A real green dot

q1.q: Can I keep my Slack status active all day?
q1.a: Yes. Green Bean holds your Slack connection during the hours you choose, so your status stays active (green dot). It runs from the cloud even with your computer off, and switches itself off once your scheduled hours end.

q2.q: How do I stop Slack from showing me as away?
q2.a: Slack flips you to away after a period without input. Green Bean maintains a connection the same way the web client does, so that switch never happens. You do not need a mouse jiggler or a script running on your machine.

q3.q: Will teammates really see me as active?
q3.a: Yes. Because it holds the same kind of connection as Slack on the web, your presence shows as active on their side.

q4.a: Credentials are stored encrypted, and messages and DMs are never read or stored. That said, any automation can be affected by your workspace's own policies.

q5.q: Does my workspace admin need to approve it?
q5.a: No. It works through your own web session, so there is no app to install and no admin approval to request.

q6.q: Can I turn it off whenever I want?
q6.a: Yes — one toggle in the dashboard stops it immediately.
